stories.title: International Court of Justice Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
stories.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar is guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority, marking a historic decision as it is the first time a state has been held accountable for genocide by the court. The ruling, passed by a narrow margin of nine votes to six, pertains to the military crackdown in 2017 that resulted in thousands of deaths and widespread displacement of the Rohingya people. The court has called for reparations and the safe return of refugees.

stories.title: Anthropic Launches Record IPO, Valued at $1.5 Trillion on Nasdaq
stories.summary: Anthropic has begun trading on the Nasdaq following a record initial public offering (IPO) that raised approximately $81.3 billion. This valuation positions the AI company at around $1.5 trillion, surpassing SpaceX's previous record of $75 billion. Despite concerns about market volatility and public sentiment towards AI, the company's shares surged upon debut.

stories.title: Leaders of China, US, and Russia Hold Historic Trilateral Talks in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin convened for a historic trilateral summit in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The leaders described the discussions as 'fruitful' and 'open and candid,' although no concrete agreements were reached. The meeting highlighted the ongoing tensions in the US-China trade war, with both Xi and Trump acknowledging the need for cooperation to safeguard world peace.

stories.title: Hakeem Jeffries Nominated for House Speaker, Poised to Make History
stories.summary: Hakeem Jeffries has been nominated by House Democrats to become the first Black Speaker of the House. In a recent secret ballot, he secured 251 votes in favor and 11 against. His nomination positions him to lead the chamber when Democrats take control in January, although he faces pressure from progressive lawmakers on key issues such as healthcare and immigration.

stories.title: Susan Smith Denied Parole Again After 32 Years for Drowning Her Sons
stories.summary: Susan Smith has been denied parole for the second time in two years, 32 years after she drowned her two sons in a South Carolina lake. During the hearing, Smith expressed regret and stated that her children 'did not deserve to die.' She was sentenced to life in prison for the 1994 drownings of 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alex.

stories.title: Voyager 1 Reaches Record Distance, Communicates from One Light-Day Away
stories.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 has successfully communicated with Earth from a distance of over 16 billion miles, equivalent to one light-day. This milestone marks the farthest any human-made object has traveled since its launch in 1977. The signal was received exactly 24 hours after it was sent from the spacecraft.
